introduction: ERC-7579 defines a minimal, interoperable interface for modular smart accounts. It standardizes four module types: validators (signature/UserOp verification), executors (autonomous execution), fallback handlers (extending the account interface), and hooks (pre/post execution checks). The standard focuses on minimal mandatory interfaces while leaving implementation flexibility, making it easier for different account providers to achieve module interoperability.
designPurpose: ERC-7579 was designed as a lighter alternative to ERC-6900 for modular account standardization. While ERC-6900 prescribes a comprehensive plugin system, ERC-7579 takes a minimal approach by defining only the essential interfaces needed for module interoperability. This makes it simpler to implement and allows account providers more flexibility in their internal architecture while still enabling cross-account module compatibility.
commonUsage: ERC-7579 is used by smart account providers including Rhinestone, Biconomy, and others building modular account ecosystems. Modules built to ERC-7579 can provide social recovery, session keys, spending limits, automated DCA strategies, and more. The standard enables a module marketplace where developers build once and users can install on any compatible account.
fn.installModule.desc: Installs a module of a specified type on the smart account. The module type determines how the module integrates (validator, executor, fallback handler, or hook).
fn.installModule.params.moduleTypeId: The type of module: 1 = Validator, 2 = Executor, 3 = Fallback, 4 = Hook.
fn.installModule.params.module: The address of the module contract to install.
fn.installModule.params.initData: Encoded initialization data passed to the module's onInstall function.
fn.uninstallModule.desc: Removes a module from the smart account. Calls the module's onUninstall function and deregisters it from the account.
fn.uninstallModule.params.moduleTypeId: The type of module to uninstall.
fn.uninstallModule.params.module: The address of the module to remove.
fn.uninstallModule.params.deInitData: Encoded data passed to the module's onUninstall function for cleanup.
fn.executeFromExecutor.desc: Called by an installed executor module to execute operations through the smart account. Supports single, batch, and delegatecall execution modes.
fn.executeFromExecutor.params.mode: The execution mode encoding: call type (single/batch/delegatecall) and execution type (default/try).
fn.executeFromExecutor.params.executionC: The encoded execution data, format depends on the mode.
fn.executeFromExecutor.returns.returnDat: Array of return data from each executed operation.
fn.isModuleInstalled.desc: Checks whether a specific module is currently installed on the account for a given module type.
fn.isModuleInstalled.params.additionalCo: Additional context bytes for the query (module-specific).
fn.isModuleInstalled.returns.installed: True if the module is installed for the specified type.
fn.accountId.desc: Returns a unique identifier string for the account implementation, typically in the format 'vendor.account.semver'.
sim.installValidator.name: Install Validator Module
sim.installValidator.desc: Install a validator module on an ERC-7579 smart account and verify it is properly registered.
sim.installValidator.step.callInstall: The account owner calls installModule(1, moduleAddress, initData) to install a validator module on the smart account.
sim.installValidator.step.hookPrecheck: If a hook module is installed, its preCheck function runs to verify the installation is authorized.
sim.installValidator.step.register: The module is registered on the account. The module's onInstall function is called with the init data to set up its internal state.
sim.installValidator.step.verify: The installation is verified by calling isModuleInstalled. The validator module is now active and will be used for signature validation.
sim.executeViaExecutor.name: Execute via Executor Module
sim.executeViaExecutor.desc: An executor module triggers an autonomous execution through the smart account.
sim.executeViaExecutor.step.trigger: The executor module is triggered (e.g., by a scheduled job or external condition) and calls executeFromExecutor on the smart account.
sim.executeViaExecutor.step.hookCheck: The hook module runs its preCheck to verify the execution is within allowed parameters (e.g., spending limits, allowed targets).
sim.executeViaExecutor.step.execute: The smart account executes the operation on the target contract on behalf of the executor module. The hook's postCheck runs after execution.
